title: Add backport-candidate labels and release-notes tags for Runtime LTS
author: Devon Price
body:
## Summary
This PR adds a consistent PR labeling taxonomy for Runtime LTS/backports/security fixes and wires the release notes generator to categorize changes based on those labels.

This is a prerequisite for:
- automated backport workflows (cherry-pick helper + bots)
- slower-change LTS release notes generation (curated summaries + stable categories)
- Support/CS visibility into whether a fix is expected to land in an LTS patch

## Motivation
We currently rely on free-form PR titles and ad-hoc labels ("bug", "perf", "security") to decide what gets cherry-picked and how it shows up in release notes. For LTS we need:
1) explicit intent (is this a backport candidate?)
2) explicit approval (is it cleared for LTS?)
3) a deterministic mapping into release note buckets
4) a lightweight schema that works across repos but is owned in the monorepo

## Label taxonomy (proposed)
### Backport/LTS flow labels
- `backport-candidate` — author signals the change may be eligible for backport (mainline PR)
- `lts-approved` — Runtime + Release Eng approved for backport to the active LTS line
- `lts-blocked` — requested for LTS but blocked pending risk/test/perf gates, or needs conflict resolution

### Security labels
- `security` — security-relevant fix (may or may not be customer-facing)
- `security-hotfix` — expedited process; use only when we are cutting an out-of-band patch (release manager adds)

### Release notes categorization labels (one required when `release-notes` is present)
- `release-notes:bugfix`
- `release-notes:performance`
- `release-notes:stability`
- `release-notes:security`
- `release-notes:build`
- `release-notes:docs`
- `release-notes:deprecation`

Notes:
- We intentionally separate "security" from the release note bucket; a security fix can land with `security` + `release-notes:security` (or omit release notes entirely if not customer-facing / embargoed).
- `lts-approved` is separate from `backport-candidate` to avoid auto-cherry-picking based solely on author intent.

## Tooling changes
- Updates the release notes generator label mapping to:
  - recognize the `release-notes:*` taxonomy
  - treat `security-hotfix` as a high-priority flag (but not required)
  - include an "LTS Backport" marker in the generated notes when the PR has `lts-approved`
- Adds a small validation step in CI for PRs labeled `release-notes` to ensure exactly one `release-notes:*` bucket is present (prevents "uncategorized" entries)

## Operational guidance
- For Runtime PRs that should appear in customer release notes, add:
  - `release-notes` + one `release-notes:*`
  - a 1–3 sentence human-written summary in the PR description under "Release notes blurb" (template added below)
- For fixes requested by Support to go into LTS, Support will reference the mainline PR and request `backport-candidate`; Runtime oncall/release manager will apply `lts-approved` after rubric review.

## Files changed (high level)
- `.github/labels.yml` — adds/normalizes labels with descriptions + colors
- `.github/pull_request_template.md` — adds "Release notes blurb" section and guidance
- `tools/release_notes/label_map.yaml` — new mapping for LTS + release note categories
- `tools/release_notes/generate.py` — uses `release-notes:*` buckets; includes LTS marker
- `tools/release_notes/validate_labels.py` — ensures category presence when `release-notes` is set
- `.github/workflows/pr-label-validation.yml` — runs validation script on labeled PRs

## Example
If a PR fixes a Sev1 crash and we want it in LTS:
- On mainline PR: `backport-candidate`, `release-notes`, `release-notes:stability`
- After review: add `lts-approved`
Generated notes will:
- include the change under "Stability"
- annotate that it is part of an LTS backport set

## Checklist
- [x] Labels defined in repo with descriptions and stable names
- [x] Release notes generator recognizes new labels
- [x] CI validation prevents missing/multiple categories
- [x] PR template updated
- [x] Documented intended use in label descriptions

## Rollout
Once merged, Release Eng will sync labels in GitHub (labels.yml is the source of truth). Existing PRs are unaffected unless labeled `release-notes` without a category.

Related:
- ENG-4823 (backport labels + automation)
- ENG-4826 (LTS release notes generator)
- SUP-18544 (request to backport KV cache crash fix into LTS)
commits: Add LTS/backport/security labels to repo label config
Add release-notes:* taxonomy and update generator mapping
Add PR label validation script + CI workflow
Update PR template with release notes blurb guidance
conversation: Connor O'Brien (review): This is the right direction. Two asks: (1) please clarify that `lts-approved` is applied by release manager/runtime lead, not authors, (2) ensure generator behavior is deterministic when multiple release-notes labels are present (fail fast).

Devon Price (author): Updated label descriptions to specify ownership (release manager/runtime lead). Added validate_labels.py and workflow to fail if `release-notes` exists without exactly one `release-notes:*` label.

Dr. Aisha Rahman (review): Naming: I prefer we keep `security` and `security-hotfix` distinct, but make sure we don’t force `release-notes:security` for embargoed items. Add a note in README about allowed combinations.
Devon Price (author): Added guidance: security fixes may omit release notes label entirely for embargoed/internal-only changes; `security-hotfix` is an expedited-process marker.
Elliot Price (review): PR template section looks good. Minor: call it “Release notes blurb” and explicitly note it can be “N/A” for non-customer-facing changes.
Devon Price (author): Done. Template updated with “N/A” guidance and examples.
Samir Qureshi (review): Can we add `release-notes:performance` vs `release-notes:stability` separation? We’ll need this for LTS to differentiate perf regressions vs correctness.
Devon Price (author): Added both `release-notes:performance` and `release-notes:stability` buckets; generator updated to render those as separate headings.
Connor O'Brien (approval): Approved. This unblocks ENG-4823/4826. Please ping #eng-releases once merged so we can sync labels and update contributor guidance.
ci_summary: PASS — build (12m), unit tests (18m), lint (6m), pr-label-validation (1m). One earlier run failed due to missing category label; fixed by adding validation + updating docs.
merge_outcome: Merged to main; labels will be synced in GitHub via labels.yml as source of truth.
